A.name: The Missed-Call Leak
A.desc: Booking-process leak angle. Emergency wildlife caller is already panicking — your site loses them at the booking button before the phone even rings. $8K-$24K/mo anchor. Tease third issue. Dual-path close.

beats.title: Cost-Led Leak Open
beats.line: Hey, my name is {caller} with CritterClick. I audit wildlife removal websites all day. Yours has a leak that's costing about $8K to $24K a month in lost jobs. Who's the best person to talk to about that?
beats.followup: Got it — give me 30 seconds and I'll show you exactly where the leak is.
beats.note: COLD open, cost-led + gatekeeper-aware. Lead with the LEAK and the $ MONTHLY cost (reason to route), then ask 'who's the best person' — works whether you hit the gatekeeper (transfer) or owner ('that's me'). Calm Miner tonality, short breath-lines, slow the last line. CritterClick register: friendly authority, no fear-mongering, no kill-talk. Anchor = ~5-10 lost jobs/wk x $400-$600 = roughly $8K-$24K/mo.

beats.title: Emergency Caller, 3-Second Window
beats.line: Here's the deal — when a homeowner hears something in the attic at night, they Google, tap the first ad, and decide in about 3 seconds whether they're calling you or moving on. Wildlife removal is emergency-service buying — that caller will hire the first shop that makes it easy to reach them. When was the last time someone on your team pulled up your site on a phone and tried to call or book right from it?
beats.followup: Yeah — that's the most common answer. The booking button is just the first leak. The bigger ones come after.
beats.note: Plain English. Emergency-service mindset. Ends with a question they can't confidently answer.

beats.title: The Booking Button Costs You the Job
beats.line: Here's what's actually happening. The homeowner taps your ad, counts to three, and your phone number isn't front and center — so they back out and tap the next shop. The next shop picks up, gets the job — and gets paid for it. The ones who do find your number land on a booking process that asks them to fill out a form before they've even said what's in their attic. By the time they figure it out, they've already called two other shops. That's the $8K to $24K a month. Getting your phone number visible and making it easy to book — those are week-one quick wins. But there's a third issue on your site that costs more than both of those combined. I'd rather show you that one with your page open.
responses: How much would this cost to fix?
beats.followup: Fair — and that's exactly what the audit answers. Pricing comes after.
beats.note: Tease the third issue. Do NOT reveal it on the call. The reveal is the audit. Dollar-anchor the competitor steal.

responses: How long does the fix take?
beats.followup: Fair — and that's exactly why I lead with the audit, not the pitch.
beats.note: Credibility frame. 100+ sites. Same checklist. Pattern recognition.

D.name: Voicemails — EURO / PAS / NEPQ
D.desc: Three ready-to-leave voicemails, one per framework: EURO (Empathy·Urgency·Reason·Offer), PAS (Problem·Agitate·Solve), and NEPQ (a curiosity question that leaves an open loop). Each is ~20-25s and drives ONE low-friction CTA: text back and I’ll send a 60-second sample of your own page. Pick one per prospect; pair with the text follow-up shown under each.

beats.title: EURO — Empathy · Urgency · Reason · Offer
beats.line: Hey, it's {caller} with CritterClick — I know you're slammed, so I'll keep this to twenty seconds. I build mobile-first pages for wildlife removal shops, and I looked at yours — it is quietly costing you jobs, around $8K to $24K a month. The reason I'm calling today and not next week is it's a fast fix, and I already put together a 60-second sample of your own page rebuilt for the phone so you can just see it. Text me back at this number and I'll send it over — no pitch, just the sample!
beats.followup: Text follow-up (send right after): “Hey it’s {caller} — just left you a quick VM. Here’s that 60-sec sample of your page I mentioned: [link]. No rush, take a look.”
beats.note: EURO = Empathy (you’re busy) → Urgency (why today) → Reason (it’s a fast fix) → Offer (the sample). Leave under ~22 seconds. Warm, fast, friendly authority — smile while you talk, no fear-talk. Say the number slowly, twice. End on the OFFER, not a goodbye.

beats.title: PAS — Problem · Agitate · Solve
beats.line: Hi, {caller} again with CritterClick. Quick one. Right now, when someone hits your site from that 11pm scratching-in-the-attic search, they're ready to book — but the page makes them work for it, so they bounce and call the next name on the list. That's not a traffic problem, that's a $8K to $24K a month leak hiding in plain sight. Good news is it's the easiest thing in the world to fix — I've got a phone-first page where one tap calls you ready to show you. Shoot me a text back and I'll send the sample!
beats.followup: Text follow-up: “{caller} here — that leak I mentioned on your VM — here’s a sample of the fix on your own page: [link]. Reply STOP if you’d rather I didn’t.”
beats.note: PAS = name the Problem → Agitate the hidden cost → Solve with the sample. The agitation is the dollar leak they can’t see, not fear. Keep it upbeat — ‘easiest fix in the world’ lands better than doom. Pause a half-beat before the dollar figure.

beats.title: NEPQ — Curiosity Question
beats.line: Hey, it's {caller} with CritterClick — one honest question and I'll let you go. If your website was quietly losing $8K to $24K a month in jobs, how would you even know? Most owners never see it — the calls just don't come, and you assume it's a slow week. I actually put together a 60-second sample of your own page rebuilt for the phone and the gap surprised me. Text this number back and I'll send it — worst case, you learn your page is already perfect!
beats.followup: Text follow-up: “That question I left you — here’s the answer: [link]. It’s a 60-sec look at your page rebuilt. Curious what you think.”
beats.note: NEPQ = a neutral, status-quo-disrupting question (‘how would you even know?’) that opens a curiosity loop the callback closes. Do NOT answer the question on the VM — the unanswered loop is what earns the call back. Tone: genuinely curious, never gotcha. The self-effacing close (‘maybe it’s already perfect’) disarms resistance.
